SEARCH ALL with ASCENDING KEY table

purpose.summary: Produces a 'Due Subscriptions Report' for a NetNews subscription system. It reads subscriber records, looks up country names via a binary search table, sorts records by country and customer name, then prints a formatted report showing subscription amounts (in local and foreign currency) grouped by country with subtotals by payment method (Visa, Access, AmExpress, Cheque) and final grand totals.

notable_features: $ SET SOURCEFORMAT"FREE" compiler directive indicating free-format source despite fixed-format column layout
SORT verb with INPUT PROCEDURE and GIVING (using a work file)
SEARCH ALL (binary search) on a table with ASCENDING KEY and INDEXED BY
Country lookup table loaded at runtime from a flat file (up to 242 entries)
EVALUATE TRUE with 88-level condition names for payment method dispatch
Currency editing pictures with floating $ sign (e.g. $$$,$$9, $$,$$$,$$9)
Exchange rate computation for local currency subscription amounts
No EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS, no COPY statements, no COMP-3 usage
verdict.notes: The AUTHOR field 'Michael Coughlan' and the comment 'CS4321-96-COBOL-EXAM' strongly suggest this is a student exam or coursework solution from 1996, likely for a university COBOL course. The program is well-structured and demonstrates solid COBOL knowledge but is clearly an academic exercise rather than production code. The $ SET SOURCEFORMAT directive is characteristic of Micro Focus or GnuCOBOL environments.
